proof_summary: Counting pairs divisible by each power \(p^i\) gives the numerator valuation \(\sum_i\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor^2\), while the factorial valuation formula turns the denominator valuation into \(\sum_i\sum_{r\le t_i} r\lfloor t_i/r\rfloor\), with \(t_i=\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor\); their difference is \(\sum_i\sum_{r\le t_i}(t_i\bmod r)\). For \(m=np+k\) with \(0\le k<p\), every \(t_i\) for \(i\ge1\) equals its value at \(np\), so this valuation formula is constant throughout the block.
